title: REL05-BP06 Make services stateless where possible
claim_or_role: Technical precedent for externalizing state so replaceable compute resources can service requests and individual-node failure is easier to tolerate.
caveat: Cloud application guidance rather than agent research; used as an architectural analogy.

title: Event Sourcing
claim_or_role: Defines event sourcing as capturing state changes as a sequence of events and discusses reconstruction temporal queries replay and parallel timelines.
caveat: Influential practitioner writing from 2005; event sourcing has real complexity and is not prescribed for every agent.

title: What do you mean by Event-Driven?
claim_or_role: Distinguishes event notification event-carried state transfer event sourcing and CQRS; supports precision about event-driven agent architecture.
caveat: Conceptual taxonomy rather than empirical evaluation.

title: Temporal Platform Documentation
claim_or_role: Contemporary example of durable execution where workflow state survives crashes outages timers and worker replacement through persisted history and replay.
caveat: Vendor documentation; demonstrates an available architecture but not independent evidence of agent correctness.

title: Durable Execution Solutions
claim_or_role: States that workflow state can be recovered replayed or paused across failures and provides task queues timers retries and persisted application state.
caveat: Vendor marketing language; use for architectural existence rather than performance claims.

title: Making retries safe with idempotent APIs
claim_or_role: Explains why retryable distributed operations need idempotent contracts to avoid repeated side effects after ambiguous failure.
caveat: General distributed-systems guidance rather than AI-specific evidence.

title: REL04-BP04 Make mutating operations idempotent
claim_or_role: Provides reliability guidance for repeated mutating requests and idempotency tokens in distributed systems.
caveat: General cloud architecture guidance; exact semantics vary by system.

title: Anthropic Economic Index report: Cadences
claim_or_role: Product telemetry and surveys showing Anthropic usage shifting from conversation toward longer-running agentic tasks and more automated work sessions.
caveat: Vendor/product-specific evidence and self-report; not representative of all workers or agent systems.

title: 2026 Work Trend Index: Agents human agency and opportunity
claim_or_role: Reports agent-intensity measures tool use orchestration depth and organizational practices around delegation and human supervision.
caveat: Company-sponsored survey of 20,000 AI-using knowledge workers in ten markets; selected population and self-report matter.

title: Task-Completion Time Horizons of Frontier AI Models
claim_or_role: Measures the human-expert task duration at which frontier agents reach specified success probabilities on a software task suite.
caveat: Task difficulty measure not literal autonomous run time; METR warns measurements above 16 hours are unreliable with its current suite.

author_or_institution: National Institute of Standards and Technology
title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework: Generative Artificial Intelligence Profile
claim_or_role: Cross-sector lifecycle risk-management guidance used for governance evaluation verification documentation and risk framing of persistent agents.
caveat: Voluntary U.S. guidance; not specific to durable agents and does not itself ensure safety.

author_or_institution: National Institute of Standards and Technology
title: AI Risk Management Framework program
claim_or_role: Shows continuing work on AI risk management and 2026 critical-infrastructure profile development.
caveat: Framework revision is ongoing; use broad lifecycle concepts rather than implying settled agent-specific regulation.

title: The LMAX Architecture
claim_or_role: Uses event sourcing and durable input history to rebuild in-memory application state after crashes; useful concrete precedent for replaceable computation plus replayable state.
caveat: Specialized architecture and historical case; should not be generalized into a universal agent design.

title: Building Durable Production-Ready Agents with the OpenAI Agents SDK and Temporal
claim_or_role: Current developer evidence that production agent builders are explicitly confronting hours-days-weeks-months execution and distributed-system failure modes.
caveat: Joint vendor framing; evidence of engineering direction rather than neutral adoption measurement.
